newsitem.title: UK: Oil prices rise in a listless market.
newsitem.headline: Oil prices rise in a listless market.

text.p: World oil prices rose on Thursday but activity on both futures and physical markets was subdued with plentiful crude oil supplies prompting potential buyers to bide their time.
December futures for benchmark crude oil Brent Blend traded 24 cents higher at $23.81 a barrel at 1530 GMT. Brokers said volume on the International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) was light.
"It's up but volumes are very light. We need to see higher volumes to confirm today's gains," a futures trader said.

Both crude oil and heating oil futures fell sharply on Wednesday in response to inventory data from the United States showing the start of a build in heating oil stocks in the world's biggest oil consuming nation.
"There is no direction or incentive to do any business," a trader said. "The market is not clear and there is a big gap between buyers and sellers."
The Brent crude market was given some encouragement by news on Thursday that production was halted at Norway's Heidrun oilfield producing 250,000 barrels per day because of technical problems.
